year.evidence: Two dates, and the register carries only the earlier. Alvarado's certificate (stamped PAGE 11): 'Certifico que siendo Gobernador de este Departamento en el ano de 1842 mande orden en dicho tiempo al Encargado de la mision de S.n Luis Obispo entonces D.n Mariano Bonilla, para que de los terrenos valdios pertenecientes a dicha mision repartiere... resultando agraciado el Indigena Romualdo con el paraje llamado el Chorro'. But the instrument actually confirmed is Pio Pico's title, stamped PAGE 17: 'Dado en el pueblo de S.n Luis Obispo... a Diez de Julio de mil ocho cientos cuarenta y seis'. Commissioner Felch expressly held (stamped PAGE 40) 'No grant was ever obtained and in truth none is pretended to have been procured from any competent authority until that signed by Pio Pico in 1846'

governor.evidence: both named officials are documented: Alvarado's own certificate of the 1842 mission-land distribution at stamped PAGE 11 ('Juan B. Alvarado Coronel de la Milicia auxiliar... Certifico que siendo Gobernador... en el ano de 1842'), and Pico's grant at stamped PAGE 17 ('Pio Pico Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de Californias... he venido en confirmar la concesion de el referido terreno', signed 'Pio Pico. Jose Matias Moreno Srio Int.o', 10 July 1846). Register's compound 'J. B. Alvarado; Pio Pico' matches the file

grantee.evidence: the file spells the grantee 'Romualdo' throughout, never 'Romaldo': expediente cover (stamped PAGE 10) 'Chorro o Huerta de Romualdo'; Alvarado cert. (stamped PAGE 11) 'el Indigena Romualdo'; his own mark on the 1846 deed (stamped PAGE 13) 'Romualdo +'; Pico's grant (stamped PAGE 17) 'Por cuanto el indigena Romualdo ha hecho constar...'; District Court decree (stamped PAGE 83) 'Huerta de Romualdo'. Right person, wrong spelling. Correctly the Indian grantee and not the U.S.-era claimant John/Juan Wilson, who bought from him in 1846

land_case.evidence: img1 red label 'CASE NO. 261 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; leaf 2 archival slip 'LAND CASE 261 SD 92 pgs.'; District Court caption (stamped PAGE 82) 'No. 261 ... Transcript from the Board of Land Commissioners No. 50'; filename cubanc_lcf_sd261.pdf

outcome.evidence: TRAP CLEARED. The Board REJECTED: stamped PAGE 3, 'San Francisco December 12' 1854. In the same case Commissioner Alpheus Felch delivered the Opinion of the Board rejecting the claim' (opinion at stamped PAGES 38-48, resting on the 10 July 1846 grant being post-conquest). Reversed on appeal: District Court decree, Judge Isaac S. K. Ogier, December Term 1856, filed 9 Feb. 1857, stamped PAGES 82-83: 'Ordered, adjudged and decreed, that the decision of said Board of Land Commissioners declaring invalid and rejecting the claim of the appellant John Wilson... be and the same is hereby reversed: And it is further ordered adjudged and decreed that the title of the appellant John Wilson to the land so claimed by him is a good and valid title, and that his claim to said land be and the same hereby is confirmed.' The United States appealed; the U.S. Supreme Court mandate, December Term 1863 (stamped PAGES 85-88), records that 'on the motion of Mr Attorney General Bates of Counsel for the Appellants, it is now here ordered adjudged and decreed by this Court that this cause be and the same is hereby dismissed', 24 March. Ogden Hoffman, District Judge, then ordered (stamped PAGE 89) 'that the claimant be allowed to proceed under the decree of this Court confirming the title to said lands as under final decree'. Register's 'Confirmed' is right and final

corrections.grantee: 'Romualdo' (Pico's grant, stamped PAGE 17: 'el indigena Romualdo'; his mark 'Romualdo +' at stamped PAGE 13). Register 'Romaldo' follows the Bancroft red label, which is itself wrong.
corrections.year: Register's 1842 is the year of the mission-land distribution certified after the fact by Alvarado (stamped PAGE 11). The title actually confirmed by the District Court is Pio Pico's of 10 July 1846 (stamped PAGE 17). A precise register entry would read '1842 (Alvarado, per later certificate); title 10 July 1846 (Pico)'.

notes: PRIORITY CASE for the 'bare Confirmed hides a Commission rejection' trap - here the trap resolves in the register's favour, but only the District Court decree of Feb. 1857 and the 1864 Supreme Court dismissal make 'Confirmed' true; the Board rejected in Dec. 1854. name.evidence: The bound volume stamped '388 SD' is NOT a rancho named Laguna. img1 red label reads verbatim: 'CASE NO. / 388 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / LANDS AND PROPERTY OF THE CATHOLIC CHURCH GRANT / JOSEPH S. ALEMANY / CLAIMANT'. Transcript title page (stamped PAGE 1): 'TRANSCRIPT OF THE PROCEEDINGS IN CASE NO. 609. Joseph S. Alemany, CLAIMANT vs. THE UNITED STATES, DEFENDANT, FOR THE PLACE NAMED Lands and property of the Catholic Church'. The journal entry at stamped PAGE 2 repeats: 'The Petition of Joseph S. Alemany ... Lands & property of the Catholic Church was presented, and ordered to be filed and docketed with No. 609'. The word 'Laguna' appears nowhere in the pages read

year.evidence: No grant decree for any place named Laguna appears in the pages read (stamped PAGES 1-9 are the case caption, the Board journal of depositions 1853-1855, and the opening of Alemany's petition). The claim in this volume is not a single dated land grant at all but a corporate claim to church property in 21 missions and 15 parishes (stamped PAGE 8)

governor.evidence: same as year - no concession decree naming a granting governor is in the pages read (stamped PAGES 1-9); this volume contains no single grant instrument

grantee.evidence: 'Bishop S. Alemany' is the U.S.-era CLAIMANT, not a Mexican grantee, and he could not have received an 1844 grant. His own petition, stamped PAGE 7, describes him as 'Joseph Sadoc Alemany, Roman Catholic Bishop of the Diocess of Monterey, in the State of California, a corporation Sole' and expressly as 'the lawful successor of the late Rt. Rev. Francisco Garcia Diego, the late Catholic Bishop of the Diocess of California, as the same existed under the former Government of this State'. The Mexican-era bishop was therefore Francisco Garcia Diego, not Alemany. This is the audit's dominant error class: the land-case claimant sitting in the grantee field

land_case.evidence: The docket string resolves to a real volume - img1 red label 'CASE NO. 388 SOUTHERN DISTRICT', every leaf stamped '388 SD', filename cubanc_lcf_sd388.pdf, 371 images - but that volume is the Catholic Church property claim (Board docket No. 609), not a rancho. Separately, the register's own scan_record_url, digicoll record 269007, titles the SAME docket 'Canada de los Pinos (also called "College Rancho," "San Isidro," "Aguichum," and "Rancho de Collegio Episcopal") [Santa Barbara County] Bishop S. Alemany, Claimant. Case no. 388, Southern District of California.' So the docket number is attached in the catalogue to a Santa Barbara rancho whose name is not Laguna either. corrections.name: SD 388 is 'Lands and property of the Catholic Church' (red label img1; transcript title stamped PAGE 1), Board docket 609, Joseph S. Alemany claimant. The Bancroft catalogue record the register itself cites (digicoll 269007) titles the same docket 'Canada de los Pinos (also called College Rancho, San Isidro, Aguichum, and Rancho de Collegio Episcopal), Santa Barbara County'. corrections.grantee: Not Alemany. His petition (stamped PAGE 7) names the Mexican-era bishop as 'the late Rt. Rev. Francisco Garcia Diego, the late Catholic Bishop of the Diocess of California'. The actual grantee of whatever grant this register row means is NOT established here - no decree was read - so Phase C must resolve it from the correct case file.

notes: HIGHEST-VALUE FINDING IN THIS CHUNK, and it needs a human decision. Three sources disagree about what 'SD 388' is: (1) the bound volume's own red label and page stamps say it is the Catholic Church property case, Board 609, Alemany claimant; (2) digicoll catalogue record 269007 - the register's own scan_record_url - titles the same docket 'Canada de los Pinos / College Rancho', Santa Barbara County, Bishop S. Alemany claimant; (3) the register calls it 'Laguna', 1844, Micheltorena, grantee Bishop S. Alemany. INFERENCE, NOT VERIFIED: the register's patent_to 'Bishop Joseph S. Alemany' matches the catalogue record's claimant, so this row probably belongs to Canada de los Pinos rather than to any 'Laguna'; do not act on that without reading the right decree. notes: CONFIRMED REGISTER ERROR, and Hoffman shares it. Hoffman's 1862 row for this case (commission 217 / court 21 - unambiguously this file) also gives the grantee as 'Miguel Abila'; the case file overrides both. This is a useful control: it shows Hoffman is not merely a screen but an actual SOURCE of at least one propagated error, so agreement between register and Hoffman must not be treated as corroboration. TWO-STAGE GRANT: (1) Micheltorena, 12 March 1844, a PROVISIONAL title of three sitios de ganado mayor expressly 'sin perjudicar los derechos que deduzcan las personas q.e tengan accion a d.ho terreno' and conditioned on compensating Mission Santa Ines (stamped PAGES 12-13); Gutierrez's receipt for 47 pesos paid to the mission is at stamped PAGE 12. (2) Pio Pico, 13 November 1845, the definitive title in property (stamped PAGES 16-17 archive copy, PAGE 19 the original). EARLIER RIVAL APPLICANTS appear in the same expediente - Damaso Rodriguez petitioning with his mother Maria Bernardina Ruiz, Monterey 7 July 1840, and her renunciation at Santa Barbara 3 Aug. 1841 (stamped PAGES 14-15) - but no Miguel Abila among them in the pages read; if 'Abila' has any basis it must lie in the 49 transcript pages not read. Expediente copies are Surveyor-General tracings certified by Sam'l D. King, 12 April 1852 (stamped PAGE 18). Register's patent_acres 48,703.91 is far larger than the three sitios granted - flag for Phase C. notes: Clean record; all six fields agree with the case file. Long pre-history documented in the expediente: Bojorquez petitioned M. G. Vallejo as Director of Colonization on 17 May 1837 and got a written licence to settle dated Sonoma 6 May 1839 (stamped PAGE 12); he petitioned Micheltorena from Sonoma 20 May 1844 (stamped PAGES 10-11) and Jacob P. Leese as Juez de Sonoma reported the land vacant 3 Sept. 1844 (stamped PAGE 11), but Micheltorena never decided; Bojorquez re-petitioned Pico 29 July 1845 (stamped PAGE 13) and got the grant. Six sitios de ganado mayor. Departmental Assembly: committee on vacant lands reported favourably 22 May 1846 (S. Arguello), Assembly approved 3 June 1846 (stamped PAGE 16). Expediente copies certified by Surveyor-General Sam'l D. King, 4 Dec. 1851 (stamped PAGE 17). ⚠ INTERNAL DATE DISCREPANCY worth flagging, though it does not disturb the year: the decree is dated 25 Nov. 1845 (stamped PAGE 13) but both copies of the titulo it orders issued are dated 21 Nov. 1845 (stamped PAGES 15, 19), and the claimant's English petition says the grant was 'made & delivered' on '5th day of November 1845' (stamped PAGE 5) while calling the decree 25 Nov. The Assembly committee read the title as dated 25 Nov. (stamped PAGE 16). Three November 1845 dates for one instrument; 1845 is safe, the day is not.
